concepts.title: Story as the Backbone of the Novel
concepts.definition: Forster holds that narration of happenings is the one factor every novel shares, however different their ambitions; he pictures it as a backbone inside the creature of the novel, carrying every higher growth on its frame.
concepts.key_idea: Strip away character, dialogue and ideas, and the sequence of events is what remains of any novel; that is why Forster calls story-telling the fundamental aspect.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww136.txt opening voice-trio and backbone/tape-worm lines
question_patterns: why does Forster call the story the fundamental aspect of the novel
how does Forster describe the place of story-telling inside a novel
what do the three voices at the start of the essay say about the novel
explain the backbone and tape-worm image used for the story
can a novel dispense with the story according to Forster
what does the essay say about readers who demand a good story

solution_steps.explain: one voice shrugs the novel off as mere busy entertainment, another swallows whole libraries of it, the third admits with a sigh that the novel tells a story

solution_steps.action: test the claim against the genre
solution_steps.explain: every novel, however experimentally written, still must present happenings one after another
the story runs through the novel like a backbone, less lovely than the limbs it supports but indispensable to them

concepts.title: Defining the Story: Time-Sequence Narrative
concepts.definition: A story, in Forster's working definition, is a narration of events arranged in their time order after knocking out the value dimension of life; judged purely as story its single merit is making the audience want to learn what happens next.
concepts.key_idea: Sequence in time is the story's only organising principle; it answers curiosity about what came after, not questions of weight or worth.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww136.txt definition passage after the Scheherazade discussion
question_patterns: define a story as Forster defines it in the essay
what is the one merit a story can claim as a story
why does Forster strip value out of his definition of story
distinguish story from plot with Forster's own kind of example
how does daily life differ from a story in its handling of time
why does Forster rate the story as the highest common factor of novels

solution_steps.explain: events arranged in their time-sequence form the story, the organ of primitive curiosity
as story it can claim only the merit of making the listener ask what happens next
life is lived by values as well as by the clock, but the story judges nothing and simply orders moments into a line

concepts.title: Scheherazade and the Ancient Appetite for Story
concepts.definition: Forster reaches back to the campfire listener tired from fighting the mammoth and to Scheherazade, who saved her life night after night by stopping each tale at dawn, to show that the hunger to know what happens next is as old as the human race.
concepts.key_idea: The cliff-hanger is a life-or-death device in the Arabian Nights frame tale, and every modern reader is still the gaping audience of that story.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww136.txt campfire and Scheherazade passages and the Arabian Nights note
question_patterns: how does the essay connect the story-telling instinct with primitive man
what device does Scheherazade use to postpone her execution
why are readers compared with Scheherazade's husband the sultan
what does the essay say about judging the sultan's curiosity
explain the reference to the one thousand and one nights in the essay
what makes the suspense of a serial tale so powerful for audiences

solution_steps.explain: the sultan's bride escapes dawn execution because her unfinished tale leaves him desperate for its ending
each sunrise break is the oldest cliff-hanger, proof that curiosity about the next event rules listeners
novel-readers queueing for the next chapter re-enact the sultan's suspense, an appetite Forster calls atavistic

concepts.title: Life in Time and by Value; the Novel's Double Allegiance
concepts.definition: Daily life seems to run on the clock yet is really shaped by value, an unmeasured intensity of moments; the novel, Forster argues, owes allegiance to both, but while a philosopher may deny time, the novelist must obey it or the story collapses.
concepts.key_idea: Memory keeps the past as a cloud of feeling, not a timetable, and the novel lives in both orders at once, ordering events in time while illuminating them with value.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww136.txt daily-life passage and the double-allegiance lines
question_patterns: what is the difference between living in time and living by value
why must a novel keep its allegiance to time even when a philosopher may deny it
how does the essay describe memory and anticipation as against the clock
what happens to a novelist who mishandles the time-sequence
explain the double allegiance of the novel according to Forster
how do experimental writers stretch or bend time in fiction

solution_steps.explain: time delivers events in sequence, value makes some instants swell and others shrink; memory stores the second, the clock the first
the good novel narrates life in time and at the same time renders life by values, never surrendering the sequence
an experimenter such as the author of Tristram Shandy or Proust with his shifting clocks still has to keep the reader sure of what followed what

worked_examples.question_pattern: In your own words, state what a story is and the single merit it can claim as a story, using Forster's reasoning.

solution_template.explain: a story is a narrative of events arranged in their time-sequence, with value knocked out
it makes the audience want to know what happens next, the merit the sultan's curiosity displays
readers are therefore like the sultan gaping at dawn for the rest of the tale

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain Forster's distinction between life in time and life by value, and why the novel must honour both.

solution_template.explain: time is the Monday-to-Tuesday order, value is the swelling of an hour into a cloud or a sun of feeling
daily life pretends to be chronological but is lived by values
the novel narrates life in time and by value together; dropping time makes it unintelligible, dropping value makes it empty
